description: Curated silicon/hardware bugs found on real NGPC hardware while developing the NgpCraft toolchain. Each entry has been validated on flash cart. Use ngpc_bug_check tool to query.

bugs.title: TLCS-900 D0 prefix mis-emitted for word register ops — D0..D7 is the WORD MEMORY family, not a word register-direct prefix
symptoms: Hang / watchdog reset
Corrupt register values
bugs.root_cause: MIS-DECODE, not a silicon fault (HW-confirmed 2026-07-03). 0xD0..0xD7 is a WORD MEMORY addressing family (e.g. `D0 B6 3F 50 00` = `cpw (0xB6),0x0050`). Word register-DIRECT is 0xD8..0xDF. The crashes below happened because the toolchain emitted a D0-prefixed byte intending a word register-immediate/ALU op, but the CPU decodes D0 as a memory access — so the operand bytes are consumed as an address and execution derails. The correct classification is toolchain mis-emission (avoid emitting D0 for register ops), not a broken opcode on silicon.
affected_instructions: cpl WA (D0 06) — toolchain intended reg-direct; CPU sees a D0 memory op
inc WA (D0 61) — any inc emitted on the D0 pattern
Any word register op the toolchain wrongly encodes with a D0 prefix (should be D8 reg-direct / E8 long)

fixes.replacement: push WA; ld WA,65535; pop HL; xor A,L; xor W,H
push WA; ld WA,0; pop HL; sub A,L; sbc W,H
extz XWA; sll N, XWA (D8 prefix safe)
ld BC,1; add A,C; adc W,B
extz xwa; ldcl dmacN, xwa (E8 long/32-bit form; D8 is the word/16-bit prefix)

notes: D1..D7 standalone are SAFE (CC900 uses them in production) — because they are WORD MEMORY forms, not register-direct.
HW-confirmed 2026-07-03: the whole D0..D7 range is the WORD MEMORY family; there is no word register-direct form there. Word reg-direct = D8..DF, long reg-direct = E8..EF.
The historic 'D0..D7 silicon-broken' label was a mis-decode/mis-emission, not a silicon defect. Fixes remain valid: never emit D0 for a word register op — use D8 (word) or E8 (long).
Since 2026-11-03 the disassembler decodes D0..D5 as word memory forms like the emulator does (`D2 AF 4D 00 61` = `incw 1,(0x004DAF)`); no `!BROKEN D0..D7` warning is emitted any more.
bugs.validation_ref: hello_j7, j10, j11 (2026-03-22 → 2026-03-24); reclassified as mis-decode 2026-07-03

bugs.title: adc W,B fails when W > 0
symptoms: Carry/overflow not propagated
Silent wrong high-byte result

fixes.replacement: Loop with W=0 so count ≤ 255, or avoid adc on W altogether

notes: With W=0 the add degenerates; values above 255 need a loop-based accumulation.

bugs.title: TLCS-900 CB-prefix byte arith/logic ALU (C-source) broken on NGPC silicon — SUB-OP-SPECIFIC (byte mul/div safe)
symptoms: Infinite loop / hang
affected_instructions: C-source byte arith/logic ALU sub-ops (add/adc/sub/sbc/and/xor/or, 0x80..0xFF range) — broken by inference from CB 81
SAFE (NOT broken): C-source byte mul/muls/div/divs, reg-reg pocket CB sub-op 0x40..0x5F, e.g. `CB 51 = div A,C` — HW-cleared 2026-07-08 (hw_test_bytediv)

fixes.replacement: add A,L (CF 81) — routes through HL (R8[7] = L)
Use CF prefix (L source) instead of CB (C source)

notes: SUB-OP-SPECIFIC: the CB (C-source) byte family is NOT broken as a whole. `CB 81 = add A,C` is a hardware-validated crash, but byte mul/muls/div/divs (CB reg-reg sub-op 0x40..0x5F) execute correctly on real NGPC — hw_test_bytediv 2026-07-08: `div A,C` (CB 51) with WA=0x1F64/C=0x64 -> WA=0x2450 (quotient 0x50, remainder 0x24). Parallels the WORD mul/div clearing (D8..DF, hw_test_muldiv 2026-07-06).
Only `CB 81` (and the arith/logic ALU sub-ops by inference) is broken; byte mul/div is confirmed safe and must NOT be flagged.
Other byte-ALU prefixes (C8 W-source, C9 A-source, CA B-source, CC D-source, CD E-source, CE H-source, CF L-source) are confirmed safe — CC900 production code uses them.
ngpc_disasm.py flags 0xCB arith/logic ALU sub-ops as `!BROKEN`, but no longer flags the byte mul/div pocket (CB 0x40..0x5F).
bugs.validation_ref: bisect_j8z13 (2026-03-22); byte mul/div cleared by hw_test_bytediv (2026-07-08)

bugs.title: link XIY with frame size N >= 5 broken on silicon
symptoms: Stack corruption after prologue
Parameters read from wrong offset
Hang on function entry

fixes.replacement: Use link XIY, 0 (max safe), allocate locals via N/2 × push WA after the link

notes: N=0..4 work. N>=5 breaks. Hard silicon limit — not a prefix problem.
t900cc.py prologue emits link XIY,0 + N/2 × push WA to stay safe.
bugs.validation_ref: bisect z10(N=8)/z11(N=6)/z12(N=5) all KO, z9(N=4) OK

bugs.title: push XSP post-decrements before push — XIY offset wrong
symptoms: Function parameters read from wrong address
Crashes shortly after prologue when params are used

fixes.op: push XIY; push XSP; pop XIY (classic frame setup)
fixes.replacement: link XIY, 0 / unlk XIY (N=0 is safe, see LINK_XIY_N_GE_5)

notes: push XSP does post-decrement — XIY ends up at S-8 instead of S-4, all params off by 4.

bugs.title: LDIRW/LDIW on NGPC use XIY (src) and XIX (dst), NOT XDE/XHL
symptoms: Block copy writes to random memory
Source read from wrong address

fixes.replacement: push XIY → push XHL; pop XIY → push XDE; pop XIX → ldirw → pop XIY

notes: Spec sheets say XDE/XHL — on silicon it's XIY/XIX. Save and restore XIY.
ngpc_memcpy_w in template uses this exact pattern.

bugs.title: DA-prefix shift with count=0 zeros the destination (not a no-op)
symptoms: Runtime shift by 0 silently clears the value
Very hard to debug — looks like random data loss

fixes.replacement: Zero-guard before shift: `or A, L` (CF E1 safe), jr Z to skip shift if count==0

notes: Guard uses A|L = count so Z is set iff count is 0. Does not clobber W or XDE.

bugs.title: t900as.py: `ei` without operand assembles to EI 7 which is effectively DI
symptoms: Joypad dead (no VBlank → BIOS never updates pad register)
No interrupt fires despite 'ei' being written

fixes.replacement: Always write `ei 0` explicitly to enable interrupts

notes: di opcode is 06 07. ei 0 is the correct enable. `ei` alone = EI 7 = DI — classic NGPC footgun.

bugs.title: `db 0xD1, 0x88` is NOT `ld WA,BC` — it's 4-byte `or BC,(mem)`
symptoms: Unexpected memory reads
Following instructions mis-decoded (bytes consumed as address)

fixes.replacement: push XBC; pop XWA

notes: Ghidra confirms D1 88 is a 4-byte opcode consuming the next 2 bytes as address.
Always use push/pop to copy register pairs.

bugs.title: t900cc.py: `const T *ptr` is not the same as `const T val` — ROM predicate must exclude PtrType
symptoms: Pointer (RAM target) gets placed in ROM
Writes via the pointer silently fail

fixes.replacement: Exclude PtrType from the is-ROMable predicate, even if the pointee type is const

notes: Example: `const u8 *s_bgm_note_table[]` — the array of pointers lives in RAM, only the bytes pointed to are const.

bugs.title: t900as.py encode_ldc() emitted wrong zz register-size values
symptoms: DMA registers never actually programmed
DMA transfers never fire or fire from wrong address

fixes.replacement: zz 0x08 → 0x10 (avoid D0 prefix)
zz 0x10 → 0x20 (E8 long word, not D8 word)

notes: ldcl dmasN,xwa now generates E8 2E cr matching CC900. Critical for DMA from ROM.

bugs.title: CC900 ABI never emits link/unlk — uses XIZ sub-regs for locals
symptoms: Generated code with link/unlk is ~10× more stack ops than CC900
Structural lag on hardware (confirmed cause of StarGunner lag)

fixes.replacement: Map C locals to XIZ sub-registers (QIZH/IZH/IZL) + push/pop XIZ at function boundary
dec N,XSP / inc N,XSP (not link/unlk)

notes: Confirmed via bisect_cc900 (2026-03-22) reverse analysis.
t900cc.py currently uses link XIY,0 + push WA — safe but ~3-5× slower than CC900.
PERF-LAG-5 (XIZ ABI) is the listed fix path.

bugs.title: t900cc.py: global `= 0` went to DATA section with ROM address instead of BSS
symptoms: Global never updates (reads constant ROM pattern)
Volatile counters frozen

fixes.replacement: Route Const(0) to bss_vars, not data_vars (applies to globals AND static locals)

bugs.title: Power button shutdown is intercepted by BIOS — user program cannot observe it
symptoms: Stub ngpc_shutdown=ret still shuts down on power button
MP_SHUTDOWN_REQ bit never readable by user code
notes: Per SysWork.txt + SysPro.txt: 'shutdown is initiated, system is shutdown before the user can evaluate the bit'.
Stub affects only TIME_SHUTDOWN_REQ (10-min idle) and BAT_SHUTDOWN_REQ (low battery) — NOT the power button.
Behavior is correct by design, not a bug — don't try to 'fix' it.

bugs.title: Toshiba cc900: crash on `s8 != s8 || s8 != s8` and on a (still-imprecise) nested-decl pattern
symptoms: Toshiba cc900 internal error on specific patterns
Does NOT affect t900cc.py — only the original Toshiba compiler

fixes.replacement: Split into separate if statements or cast to int

fixes.op: nested-block decl pattern (precise reproducer not captured)
fixes.replacement: If you hit a cc900 internal error inside a nested block, try moving the declaration to the function top and assigning inside the block

notes: S8 OR chain is well-attested and lintable (HW-3c).

The 'nested decl' part of this bug entry is too vague — likely refers to mixed declarations and statements (C99 extension), but we don't have a precise failing snippet. The HW-3d lint was added then removed because pure depth-based detection false-positived on valid C89 (decls at top of inner blocks like for-body). To re-enable a lint, capture an exact failing snippet on cc900 and narrow the detection.

bugs.title: Large static-like locals must be moved to file-scope BSS (stack too small)
symptoms: Stack overflow → random corruption
Works on emulator, crashes on real hw with full DMA tables

fixes.replacement: Move to file-scope static — they go to BSS and don't cost stack

notes: Example: s_bg_dma_phase_x[32][76] = 2432 bytes. Stack was 210 → 2643 bytes after moving. Fix #23.

bugs.opcode_pattern: C: RGB(r, g, b) with u8 arguments
bugs.title: RGB() built from u8 components loses the blue nibble -- cc900 evaluates `<< 8` in 8-bit width
symptoms: Every colour on screen is wrong while the data and the palette writes are correct
An orange background renders green, a warm gradient turns cyan
Palette RAM holds the right low byte and a zero high byte
notes: `(b) & 0xF` on a u8 stays 8-bit, so the `<< 8` term is always zero. Widen each component to u16 BEFORE shifting, which is what the NGPC C Framework 0.4 macro did.
Typical trigger: converting an RGB444 export, RGB((u8)(v & 0xF), (u8)((v >> 4) & 0xF), (u8)((v >> 8) & 0xF)).
Affects the NgpCraft base template's ngpc_hw.h as shipped.
Diagnosis that settled it in one measurement: write a known constant (0x0ABC) into an unused palette slot. It arrived intact, which cleared the write path and pointed at the computed value.
bugs.validation_ref: measured on two emulated consoles (palette RAM compared byte for byte with a known-good ROM), 2026-07-26

bugs.title: Palette RAM takes 16-bit accesses only, and entry 0 must be left alone
symptoms: Colours keep their low byte and lose the high nibble
Writing colour 0 changes what shows through a scroll plane

fixes.op: palette write helper as a macro
fixes.replacement: keep it a FUNCTION taking u16 parameters: that is what makes cc900 emit word stores

fixes.op: SetPalette(plane, id, c0, c1, c2, c3)
fixes.replacement: write colours 1..3 only; entry 0 is the transparent slot

notes: The original NGPC C Framework SetPalette() forwarded to SetColors() precisely to skip entry 0.
Scroll palettes: SPR 0x8200, SCR1 0x8280, SCR2 0x8300, BG 0x83E0; 4 u16 per palette.
bugs.validation_ref: measured on emulated hardware while porting a game between two SDKs, 2026-07-26

bugs.opcode_pattern: C: sprite control byte, priority field
bugs.title: Sprite priority 0 means HIDDEN -- a sprite set up without a priority never appears
symptoms: One sprite is invisible while the game logic using it keeps running normally
The object still collides and still scores; only the drawing is missing

fixes.replacement: ngpc_sprite_set(id, x, y, tile, pal, SPR_FRONT)   /* or the priority you mean */

notes: OAM control byte: bits 4-3 priority (0 = hidden, 3 = front), bit 7 H-flip, bit 6 V-flip, bits 2-1 chaining.

The NGPC C Framework's SetSprite() always wrote control register 24 (front) and added 6 for chaining, so ports that forward a flags value of 0 lose exactly the sprites that had no explicit SpriteControl() call after them.
bugs.validation_ref: measured on two emulated consoles (OAM entry compared with a known-good ROM), 2026-07-26

bugs.title: COMINIT installs the BIOS serial handlers at 0x6FE4/0x6FE8 -- do not reinstall user vectors afterwards
symptoms: Exactly one byte leaves the console, then the TX ring stays full
The link looks like 'cable unplugged' although bytes reach the wire

fixes.op: save 0x6FE4/0x6FE8 at boot and restore them after opening the link
fixes.replacement: do nothing: COMINIT writes the correct handlers itself

notes: SDK init routines that fill every user vector with a dummy handler are harmless as long as they run BEFORE the link is opened.
Saving those two pointers at boot and 'restoring' them later overwrites the working handlers -- the ring then never drains.
bugs.validation_ref: measured on emulated hardware with the retail BIOS, 2026-07-25

bugs.title: cc900 without -A emits a NARROW hardware divide for % and / -- quotient overflow makes the result indeterminate (works on emulators, breaks on console)
symptoms: Shuffle / random index out of range on real hardware only
Array read/written out of bounds after `x % n` with a small n
Game behaves differently on console and emulator from the same seed
Crash or corrupted state that no emulator reproduces
bugs.root_cause: Without the -A (ANSI) option, cc900 does not widen operands for multiply/divide: `u16 % u8` compiles to a 16/8 `div BC,H` (bytes CE 53), `u32 % u16` to a 32/16 `div XWA,..`. The quotient must fit in the low half (8 or 16 bits); when it does not (e.g. 38457 % 71: quotient 541 > 255) the CPU sets V and the destination is INDETERMINATE (Toshiba cc900 manual, section 3.12.2 'Arithmetic Conversion of Multiplication and Division', Example 2 + Caution). The remainder is then used as an index with no check.
affected_instructions: `u16_value % u8_count` (typical: xorshift/LCG state % loop counter in a shuffle)
`u16_value / u8_value` when the quotient can exceed 255
`u32_value % u16_value` / `u32 / u16` when the quotient can exceed 65535
Disassembly signature: `div BC,H` = CE 53 (older disassemblers printed `div HL,H`)

fixes.replacement: Compile the file with -A (ANSI arithmetic: cc900 then emits a 32/16 divide with zero-extension) -- check the other expressions of the file, -A changes them too
Reduce without div: 16 shift/subtract steps on a u16 remainder (no RAM, no call)
Two narrow divides whose quotients always fit: `u8 hi = (u8)((u8)(state >> 8) % n); r = (u8)((((u16)hi << 8) | (u8)state) % n);` -- the second dividend is < n*256, so its quotient is < 256

notes: Casting only the divisor to u16 is NOT enough: cc900 still emits the 16/8 `div BC,H`.

Emulators usually compute the remainder with the host `%` even when the quotient overflows (they only raise V), so the bug is invisible there. Always look at the emitted asm (`cc900 -S`) of any % in a shuffle or index computation.
u8 % u8 is safe (the quotient of an 8-bit dividend always fits in 8 bits).
Same manual section 3.12.1: without -A, char + char is computed in char -- see CC900_CHAR_ARITH_8BIT.
bugs.validation_ref: Toshiba cc900 manual 3.12.2 (documented behaviour); emitted asm checked with cc900 -O3 -Nb2 without -A

bugs.opcode_pattern: u8 + u8 / u8 * const / int constant
bugs.title: cc900 without -A computes char arithmetic in char: u8 + u8 and u8 * const lose their carry; int constants are 16-bit
symptoms: Works up to a value, then breaks (a threshold symptom)
An increment that becomes zero above a speed / count
A computed constant silently zero
bugs.root_cause: Toshiba cc900 manual 3.12.1 Caution: without -A, the addition of two char operands is done in char and only then converted. `(u16)(frac + speed)` with two u8 adds on 8 bits (asm: `add C,(XSP+4)` then `extz BC`). `n * 30u + 50u` with n u8 is computed on 8 bits. And an int is 16 bits: `512 * 256` folds to 0.

fixes.replacement: (u16)((u16)a + (u16)b) -- cast EVERY operand
(u16)n * 30u + 50u -- cast the FIRST operand
compute in two steps or with UL

notes: A symptom that depends on a value threshold is a width symptom: compile a minimal fragment with `cc900 -S` before suspecting the logic.
bugs.validation_ref: Toshiba cc900 manual 3.12.1; measured on a shipped ROM (scenery step froze above a speed threshold)

bugs.title: Bit 7 of the joypad byte 0x6F82 is NOT the power switch -- a 'hold POWER to shut down' fallback powers consoles off
symptoms: Console powers off cleanly (black screen, like the switch) at an unexpected moment
Shutdown that no emulator reproduces
bugs.root_cause: SNK SysWork.txt: Sys_Lever (0x6F82) bit 6 = OPTION (button C of the development controller), bit 7 = button D of that controller. The power switch is only visible through User_Shutdown (0x6F85, bit 7 switch, bit 6 inactivity, bit 5 low battery). Template code that defines PAD_POWER = 0x80 and calls shutdown after bit 7 is held N frames shuts the console down whenever that bit reads 1.

fixes.replacement: Remove it. Honour only 0x6F85 (and show which bit fired before shutting down).

notes: See also POWER_BUTTON_BIOS_HANDLED: the real switch is handled by the BIOS.

bugs.title: I/O 0x6E is WDMOD and 0x6F is WDCR (watchdog) -- NOT a cartridge /WE control; never write WDMOD around a flash stub
symptoms: Flash code commented 'assert /WE' that actually reconfigures the watchdog
Console switches itself off during a save that erases a block, at random (one erase in two); no system power request (0x6F85 clear), the target block not even erased; never reproduced on an emulator
bugs.root_cause: Toshiba IO900H.H (the 900/H header of the SDK): `WDMOD 0x6e` (watchdog mode), `WDCR 0x6f` (watchdog control; 0x4E = clear, 0xB1 = disable code). The common flash stub prologue `ld (0x6E),0x14 / ld (0x6F),0xB1` is the two-step WATCHDOG DISABLE (clear WDTE in WDMOD, then B1 to WDCR), not a bus write-enable. Headers for other chips of the family (IO900.H, IO900L.H) place WDMOD at 0x5C -- wrong for this machine.
affected_instructions: ld (0x6E),0xF0 ; 'deassert /WE' (watchdog back on with a FIXED mode)

fixes.replacement: di (save SR first); NEVER write WDMOD (0x6E); ld (0x6F),0x4E right before and right after the call; erase stub clears the watchdog inside its wait loop: insert 08 6F 4E (ld (0x6F),0x4E) at offset 0x35 of the 98-byte StarGunner-style stub and re-aim the backward jump 66 ED -> 66 EA (101 bytes, copy length 0x65); restore SR

notes: The earlier advice (clear first, save WDMOD, disable, restore the saved mode) was an untested hypothesis; the disable/re-enable pair itself is what switched consoles off.
Rare erases hide it: append-only slots that erase once every ~30 saves can ship unseen; a save that fills a block erases on every save and meets it at once.
8 KB erase measured ~57 ms on a cartridge vs a ~100 ms watchdog; a modern flash cart can be slower -- clearing inside the wait loop makes the length irrelevant.
bugs.validation_ref: Console, 2026-10-17, modern flash cart: block erases with the watchdog switched off killed the console one erase in two; with WDMOD never written and the loop-clearing stub, repeated erases and the game's real save pass. Toshiba IO900H.H (SDK t900 CUSTOMIZ/C900_H); TMP95C061 datasheet section 3.13 (watchdog)

bugs.opcode_pattern: flash erase/write stub / ei after flash
bugs.title: Flash erase/write wrappers: interrupts must stay masked for the whole operation, SR restored (not `ei`), status returned and verified
symptoms: Crash / power-off during a save on real hardware only
Save 'succeeds' (game continues) but is not there after power-on
bugs.root_cause: While the NOR chip programs or erases it answers status instead of contents to every read of the cartridge window. Running the stub from RAM does not protect a VBlank ISR that lives in ROM: if an interrupt fires, the CPU fetches instructions from the busy chip. SNK SysCall.txt: all interrupts are prohibited during flash system calls; the SWI 1 path masks them. A wrapper without `di` works most of the time in emulators (the busy window is ~200 cycles/byte, an interrupt rarely lands in it).
affected_instructions: `ei` at the end of the wrapper (forces interrupts on instead of restoring the caller's state)
ignoring the stub's return value (erase failed -> still writes slot 0)
slot judged free on its first byte only
unknown cartridge capacity (0x6C58 = 0) treated as 16 Mbit

fixes.replacement: push SR; di; ...; pop SR  (restore, do not force ei)
return the stub status to C; abort on failure; verify 8 KB = 0xFF after erase and the 512 bytes after programming
a slot is free only if all 512 bytes are 0xFF
unknown 0x6C58 value -> do not save (and show it)

notes: 'The game continues' does not prove a save happened: re-read after a power cycle (or a fresh emulator instance).

Hardware reports: build ONE binary, derive variants that differ by one byte (save disabled / fix A / fix B), test each separately on the same cartridge and initial save state. Padding a ROM with 0xFF does not change its prefix -- compare images before blaming the padding.
bugs.validation_ref: SNK SysCall.txt (flash calls prohibit interrupts); flash busy-window measurements in Storage-and-Saves 5.0c

bugs.opcode_pattern: D7 FA / C7 xx / E7 xx
bugs.title: C7 / D7 / E7 are the extended-register escapes -- `D7 FA 04` is `push QIZ`, not an invalid byte pair
symptoms: A disassembler flags `D7 FA` in function prologues as invalid/suspect
bugs.root_cause: `11zz0111` (C7 byte, D7 word, E7 long) is followed by an 8-bit REGISTER CODE, then the operation byte: the same register instruction set as C8+r/D8+r/E8+r, able to name upper halves (QWA..QIZ), IX/IY/IZ/SP bytes and other banks. Code map: E0..FF current bank (group=(code>>2)&7, byte pos=code&3), D0..DF previous bank, below D0 absolute bank=code>>4. 0xFA = XIZ, byte position 2 = QIZ. cc900 saves QIZ with `D7 FA 04` / restores with `D7 FA 05` in ordinary prologues.

fixes.op: converting locals to static because of a D7 FA alert
fixes.replacement: Do not. The encoding is valid; converting locals costs RAM (a static per local) and changes reentrancy.

notes: ngpc_disasm decodes these escapes since 2026-09-28; older builds printed `rl A,SP ; !SUSPECT` followed by an unknown byte.
bugs.validation_ref: Official Toshiba assembler encodings (asm900); cc900 -S output
